lenses.title: Correctness
lenses.focus: Does the change do what the diff, its comments and its description say it does? Read the claim and the code as two independent assertions and look for the gap between them. Prefer a concrete failing input over a description of a risk. This dimension judges work performed against a claim about it, not a description of a requirement: where the change under review is itself a description of a requirement, there is no behaviour yet for this lens to check — answer out_of_scope rather than manufacturing a gap between a description and work that does not exist yet.

lenses.title: Honesty of the record
lenses.focus: Anything that reports a state it did not observe: a comment claiming a property the code does not have, a log line or return value describing work that did not happen, a success reported over an empty result, documentation asserting a behaviour the implementation lacks. This still applies in full where a description of a requirement makes a false claim about the system's CURRENT state — that is exactly as dishonest there as anywhere else. But a description of a requirement is not dishonest merely for reporting no success — the absence of a completion claim is not itself a finding, and must not be written up as one.

lenses.title: Failure distinguishable from silence
lenses.focus: Where the change can fail, can a reader tell which failure happened? Missing, empty and broken must stay three answers. A swallowed error, a catch that returns a default, or a single word covering two outcomes belongs here. This judges error handling that exists in the change. A description of a requirement has no catch, return or logged outcome yet — answer out_of_scope, not a review of prose about intended handling as though it were the handling itself.

lenses.title: Verification that verifies
lenses.focus: Would each new or changed test fail if the code it covers were wrong? Look for assertions that hold vacuously, suites that pass because they found nothing to run, and guards whose only test exercises the pure function underneath rather than the guard. This judges a test that exists in the change. A description of a requirement — including one describing what a future test must prove — has no test yet for this lens to check against; answer out_of_scope, not a verdict on a stated intention.

lenses.title: Scope, collateral and credentials
lenses.focus: What does this change touch that it did not need to touch? Reformatting, drive-by renames, widened permissions, a credential reaching a wider process than before, or a bound that moved without being named.
